title: Drop-off Waterfall Analysis
insights:
Analysis of Bus Ticket Booking App Drop-off Patterns

The dataset contains a total of 44,031 events recorded from 499 users between December 24, 2025, and January 20, 2026. The analysis focuses on user drop-off rates across the booking flow stages.

a) WORST TRANSITION

The stage that loses the most users is from Results to Seat Selection, with a total of 173 users lost, representing a drop-off rate of 45.6%.

b) REVENUE IMPACT

Estimating potential bookings lost at the worst transition (Results to Seat Selection), if we assume an average ticket price of $50, the revenue impact can be calculated as follows:

  • Lost users: 173
  • Potential bookings lost: 173 x $50 = $8,650

c) ROOT CAUSES

Two to three likely UX/technical reasons for the high drop-off from Results to Seat Selection include:

  • Complex Seat Selection Interface: Users may find the seat selection process confusing or cumbersome, leading to frustration and abandonment.
  • Insufficient Information on Bus Options: Lack of clear information regarding bus options or seat availability may deter users from proceeding.
  • Technical Glitches: Any lag or errors during the transition from results to seat selection could cause users to abandon the process.

d) FIXES

Three specific UX improvements ranked by expected impact are:

  • Simplify Seat Selection Process: Streamlining the seat selection interface to make it more intuitive and user-friendly could significantly reduce drop-offs.
  • Enhance Information Display: Providing clearer information about bus options, seat availability, and pricing during the results stage can help users make informed decisions.
  • Improve System Performance: Ensuring that the app runs smoothly without technical glitches during critical transitions will enhance user experience and reduce abandonment rates.
